confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from crowd-sourced, undated or mixed-city sources, mainly Sydney and Melbourne proxies, not Newcastle-specific data. Beer is based on a 0.5L Newcastle draught figure (about AUD 13.29) scaled to a 425ml serving. Cocktail and wine_glass are estimates: no 2026 Newcastle cocktail or wine-by-the-glass price was found, so cocktail uses Melbourne/Sydney averages discounted for Newcastle, and wine_glass is set at roughly the schooner-to-house-wine ratio seen in Melbourne listings. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge and the Newcastle regional context, not from live listings; July is winter, which may ease beach-town rates. FX caveat: the only RBA observation I could tie to an rba.gov.au page in the results was AUD/USD 0.7088 at 4.00 pm on 2026-03-20. Later figures reported by secondary sites (for example about 0.672 for 2026-11-18) could not be verified against rba.gov.au, so I did not use them. The source rate is therefore older than the generation date, and the USD anchors were converted at about 0.68 USD per AUD, which sits between the November market reports and the verified March observation.
comparable_city_reasoning: Oceania basis using Australian mid-sized coastal city price levels. Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are informed by national and Melbourne/Sydney aggregated price reports, adjusted down for Newcastle relative to the Sydney/Melbourne premium. Cocktail is based on Melbourne and Sydney average cocktail prices, adjusted down. Wine_glass uses the beer-relative basis described in confidence_notes. Accommodation uses a model estimate without accommodation searches.
